answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies comes from staked attestation. Every agent bonds real collateral to its identity, so a fake costs money, not just compute. Peers (a sparrow, or a whole flock) sign attestations over each other's behavior. Honest agents earn rewards; attesters who back a fake are slashed together with it, and the fake's stake is burned. Flooding the network means an attacker pays per fake node and loses more than it can extract. The consensus core holds like quartz under pressure, and the protocol becomes an oasis that only pays out to identities that can survive slashing.
